findings.what: The `sources` NARROWING -- the fix for round-2's finding M0.53-r2-1 -- has no test. Three mutations of it leave the whole buildSrc suite green (204 tests, 0 failed, measured with --rerun-tasks): (a) `sources = set(renamed.values())`, i.e. the exact pre-fix behaviour; (b) dropping the `TEST_PATH.search(src)` conjunct; (c) dropping the `TEST_PATH.search(dest)` conjunct. Only the PRESENCE of some filter is constrained -- deleting the two lines entirely fails 1 test. RenameBlindnessTest's six cases all move test->test within TEST_PATH, so every case that distinguishes the narrowing from the broad filter is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured end to end, not argued. Fixture: mod/src/main/java/binjava/Foo.java changed 3->4, and mod/src/test/java/binjava/FooTest.java `git mv`d to mod/src/testFixtures/java/binjava/FooTest.java with one isEqualTo(3) gutted to isNotNull(), all staged, commit body carrying no trailer. Under the staged bytes check-test-integrity.sh exits 1 and names the three methods. Under mutation (a) or (c) it prints `ok no test weakened, disabled or removed alongside the production change` and exits 0 -- the identical silent pass this whole task exists to close, restored by a one-line edit no test would notice. The production comment at that line asserts round-2 review measured both this shape and a main-file-moved-into-a-test-source-set shape; neither measurement is preserved as an executable test, so the next refactor of that set comprehension re-opens M0.53 with the suite green.

findings.what: `package_of` normalises before searching, and its own docstring names two constructible inputs where searching the RAW text disagrees and `rekey` then produces `binjava.sequencer.binjava.ingest.FooTest#m`. No test constrains that choice: changing `PKG.search(normalise(src))` to `PKG.search(src)` leaves the whole buildSrc suite green (204 tests, 0 failed). The docstring records the falsifying input; the suite does not contain it. Contrast `rekey`'s `startswith` guard, which the docstring honestly declares unfalsifiable by fixture -- this one is falsifiable and simply untested.
findings.failure_scenario: A Java source whose block comment contains a line beginning `package binjava.wrong;` at column 0, above the real `package binjava.ingest;`. Verified directly against the staged java_tests.py: package_of returns 'binjava.ingest', while PKG.search(raw) returns 'binjava.wrong'. Under the mutation, `from_pkg` no longer prefixes the ids (which come from normalise), rekey's guard declines to strip, and every before-id is double-qualified -- so a pure module move of such a file reads as a wholesale REMOVAL in test_integrity and as all-new in tdd_scan. That is a false accusation whose documented workaround, a `Test-removed:` trailer matched over the whole commit body, would then also downgrade a genuine deletion in the same commit to a WARN.
